feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
The discussion raises questions regarding the necessity of the SIGHASH_SCRIPTMASK flag, highlighting its apparent redundancy. The inquiry suggests that mask-removal could be consistently applied during signing procedures, as any situation involving the signing of arbitrary scripts likely indicates deeper issues or risks. The implication is that the presence of this flag might not provide additional security or functionality and could instead complicate the process.
In the context of Taproot, further confusion is expressed about the relevance of scriptmask. Taproot introduces an approach where alternate scripts remain both hidden and flexible, which seems to diminish the need for mechanisms like scriptmask. This new paradigm potentially renders certain legacy features obsolete, prompting a reevaluation of their role within updated transaction protocols. The questions emphasize the importance of clarity and efficiency in cryptographic signing practices as Bitcoin evolves.
